sources.citation: Walker, Dale F. 1976. A Grammar of the Lampung Language: the Pesisir Dialect of Way Lima. NUSA 2. Jakarta: Badan Penyelenggara Seri NUSA.
sources.note: Already downloaded (kome1238 folder) - comparison only: sec. 2.41 p. 5 gives final-syllable, very slight, non-contrastive word stress for Way Lima Lampung (lamp1243); Abdurrahman & Yallop 1979 place Komering with Way Lima in the Pesisir grouping, but this is not a Kayu Agung statement.

sources.citation: Afria, Rengki; Dimas Sanjaya; Mesha Tiara. 2020. Leksikostatistik dan Grotokronologi Bahasa Melayu Palembang, Basemah Lahat, Basemah Pagaralam, dan Kayu Agung: Kajian Linguistik Historis Komparatif. Madah: Jurnal Bahasa dan Sastra 11(1): 27-42. doi:10.31503/madah.v11i1.223
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistics only (Kayuagung = the Ogan Komering Ilir lect, p. 28). No tekanan/aksen/intonasi anywhere.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (id) 'Bahasa Kayuagung'; Wikipedia (en) 'Komering language'; blog posts word-dialect.blogspot 2012 'Bahasa Komering, Kayu Agung Asli' and Kompasiana 2011 'Bahasa Kayuagung secara garis besar'.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; the blog gives a phonetic wordlist for Kayu Agung Asli without any statement on accent. Wikipedia cites only Glottolog, Adelaar 2005, Walker 1975/1976 and Abdurrahman & Yallop 1979.

sources.citation: Anderbeck, Karl. 2007 [10-ICAL 2006]. An initial reconstruction of Proto-Lampungic: phonology and basic vocabulary. 115 pp. (later Studies in Philippine Languages and Cultures 16).
sources.note: Historical segmental phonology; Kayu Agung Asli (KAAsli) and Kayu Agung Pendatang (KAPend, Paku village) are two of the wordlists (sec. 2.3.1: *e > o in ultimate syllables along the Komering incl. both Kayu Agung lects). The word 'stress' does not occur; no accent statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-195: merge [vky] Kayu Agung into [kge] Komering (submitted by Karl Anderbeck, SIL Indonesia; supporter Charlie Hanawalt). Adopted 2008-01-14.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 4(b): two lects in Kayu Agung town, 'Kayu Agung' (dominant, said to come from Lampung) and 'Kayu Agung Asli' (one village), with 'well-known but minor differences.. in terms of lexicon and phonology'; both intelligible with upstream Komering. Cites Hanawalt et al. forthcoming (SIL Electronic Survey Report), Anderbeck 2006, Walker 1975.

sources.citation: Gani, Zainal Abidin; Yazid Yan; Natidjah Sj; Nazlimi Nawawi. 1986. Morfologi dan Sintaksis Bahasa Kayu Agung. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. viii+166 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Daftar Isi (pp. vii-viii): Bab 1 Pendahuluan, Bab 2 Morfologi (2.1 Ejaan, 2.2 Morfofonologi, 2.3 Wujud Morfem..), Bab 3 Sintaksis, Bab 4 Kesimpulan; no phonology chapter; no occurrence of tekanan/aksen/suprasegmental/intonasi/prosodi. Sec. 1.4.1 p. 3: two dialects, 'dialek asli' (dusun Kayu Agung) and 'dialek dusun'; the sample is dialek dusun. Bibliography p. 165 cites 'Dunggio, P.D. et al. 1977. Struktur Bahasa Kayu Agung' (project report later printed 1984).

sources.citation: Saleh, Yuslizal; Aidy Ruslan; Hasbi Yusuf; Sofyan Silahiddin; Achyar Burhan. 1984. Morfologi Kata Kerja Bahasa Komering. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. 310 pp.
sources.note: Komering Ulu dialects (Buay Madang, Cempaka, Belitang; Martapura-Simpang), not Kayu Agung. Sec. 3.3 pp. 20-21: the only suprasegmental phoneme is open juncture; 'tekanan' occurs only in a general-theory paragraph (p. 12, Simalungun example). No placement statement. Kayu Agung is mentioned once (p. ~13) as a neighbouring language.

sources.citation: Abdurrahman, Sofjan & Colin Yallop. 1979. A brief outline of Komering phonology and morphology. NUSA 7: 11-18. Jakarta: Badan Penyelenggara Seri NUSA.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/intonation: no hits; the kome1238 pass and its second reader read secs. 2.1-2.10 in full). Describes Komering Ulu (Adumanis), not Kayu Agung.

sources.citation: Peta Bahasa (Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa), entry 'Kayu Agung' (idb=29), petabahasa.kemendikdasmen.go.id; mirrored on id.wikibooks 'Bahasa Kayu Agung'.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Lists nine 'dialects' (Lintang, Kimak, Pagar Dewa, Pematang, Penesak, Kayu Agung Perigi, Kikim, Lubuk Rumbai, Ngulak) across Lahat, Empat Lawang, Muara Enim, OKU etc. with 51-80% dialectometric difference; this is a different (largely Malayic) bundle from the Lampungic Kayu Agung [vky].
